records.coverage_note: All three acts of the regest are covered: the earlier donation of Kemnade and Fischbeck to Corvey (no donor, no date, correct), the Fürstenspruch by Bischof Burchard, and Friedrich's accession joined by rf:refersToAct. Actor identifications follow the packet (B001563, C000961; shared ruler for Friedrich, no competing candidate). The substantive content of the Spruch, freedom from all imperial services, survives only in the evidence text.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22652:beitritt
findings.description: Friedrich's accession (Beitritt) to a judgment is typed rv:Confirmation with role rv:Grantor. Accession or assent is not a confirmation of possession or rights; the extractor flagged this as a model gap in its comment. Acceptable as the nearest available type, but a later query for confirmations will over-count.
findings.evidence_quote: tritt einem von Bischof Burchard von Straßburg gefällten Fürstenspruch bei
findings.proposed_correction: Keep for this run; add an assent/accession act type and an assenting-party role to the vocabulary and retype.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22652:fuerstenspruch
findings.description: The decisive content of the judgment, that the Stifte remain free of all imperial services, is not represented by rf:concerns on a right or exemption; the factoid concerns only the two Stifte. rv:RightTypes has no immunity or exemption concept, so this is a model gap rather than an extraction error. The temporal word 'auch weiterhin' is correctly kept as rf:qualifier.
findings.evidence_quote: auch weiterhin frei von allen Reichsdiensten sein sollen
findings.proposed_correction: Add an exemption/immunity concept to rv:RightTypes and attach an E30_Right labelled 'frei von allen Reichsdiensten' via rf:concerns.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22652:fuerstenspruch
findings.description: The judgment's evidence starts inside the accession clause and includes the verb particle 'bei' of Friedrich's act; the shortest passage carrying the judgment would begin at 'einem von Bischof Burchard' and could omit 'bei'. Cosmetic.
findings.evidence_quote: einem von Bischof Burchard von Straßburg gefällten Fürstenspruch bei, nach dem
findings.proposed_correction: None needed; optionally split into two selectors without 'bei'.

model_gaps: No act type for assent or accession to another actor's act (Beitritt).
No right type for exemption or immunity from imperial services (frei von allen Reichsdiensten).

records.coverage_note: The parenthood between Herzog Friedrich II. (F000681) and Friedrich (shared ruler) is correctly extracted with the kinship word in rf:qualifier. The central statement of the regest, the succession in the duchy of Swabia, is not recorded; the extractor documented this as a model gap.

findings.description: The succession in the Herzogtum Schwaben is the main content of the regest and is omitted. The act scheme has no succession type, so the act itself is a model gap, but the contract could have recorded part of it: rv:Appointment is defined as Einsetzung in ein Amt, or a rf:StateFactoid rv:OfficeHolding with Friedrich as rv:Officeholder, rf:concerns the place Herzogtum Schwaben (candidate S000398) and rf:qualifier 'folgt ... nach' in exact wording. The father as predecessor would need a role the vocabulary lacks.
findings.evidence_quote: Friedrich folgt seinem Vater, Herzog Friedrich II., im Herzogtum Schwaben nach.
findings.proposed_correction: Add a factoid for the succession: either rv:Appointment with Friedrich as rv:Recipient and the father as rv:Participant, or rv:OfficeHolding for Friedrich concerning <urn:regesta:actor:RI004-002-S000398> (E53_Place 'Herzogtum Schwaben'), with evidence the full sentence; report succession and predecessor role as model gaps.

model_gaps: No act type for succession in an office or lordship, and no predecessor/successor role.

records.coverage_note: Both acts are covered: the earlier handover of the Bamberger Ministerialien by Bischof Eberhard to the king, with the reason in exact wording as rf:ground, and the king's committal of the Ministerialien to the duke's protection with the Latin reservation 'non in ius advocatię' as rf:exception and a Protection right. Actors E000011, K000316 and B000133 match the packet. Findings concern identification, unreferenced actors and role choices, none of them unsupported by the text.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:actor:RI004-002-F000471
findings.description: 'Herzog Friedrichs von Schwaben' is identified with the shared ruler although candidate F000681 (Herzog von Schwaben, father of Barbarossa) also matches by name and title. The candidate carries only role p_komment, not nennung, which supports reading the summary's duke as the ruler; the extractor flagged the identification as a reading. Defensible, but it rests on the candidate role, not on the summary text.
findings.evidence_quote: dem Schutz Herzog Friedrichs von Schwaben
findings.proposed_correction: Keep; list as an unresolved identity for expert review (shared ruler versus F000681).

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22654:uebergabe
findings.description: Konrad von Rietfeld (K000502) and Berengar von Albeck (B000529) are named in the summary and have matching candidates, but appear only inside the rf:ground literal, so the graph cannot find them. The oppression has no act type (rv:Dispute does not fit), and no role covers an oppressor in a reason clause.
findings.evidence_quote: wegen ihrer Bedrückung durch Konrad von Rietfeld und Berengar von Albeck
findings.proposed_correction: Optionally add references with rv:Participant to the handover factoid, or report the oppression as a model gap so the two actors are at least listed.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22654:schutzunterstellung
findings.description: The protected Ministerialien are rv:Beneficiary and the duke rv:Recipient; this is a reasonable reading (the duke receives the charge, the Ministerialien benefit), but the Latin 'in manus ... commisit' makes the Ministerialien the object handed over. rf:refersToAct is defined for confirmations or assurances referring to an earlier act; here it links a consequent act to its precondition, a stretch of the property. Typing the bishop's handover of persons as rv:Grant (transfer of a right, possession or institution) is also an approximation.
findings.evidence_quote: die ihm von Bischof Eberhard (II.) wegen ihrer Bedrückung durch Konrad von Rietfeld und Berengar von Albeck übergeben worden sind
findings.proposed_correction: Keep for this run; consider a sequence relation distinct from rf:refersToAct and a commendation or handover type for persons in the next contract.

model_gaps: No act type for oppression or violence that a reason clause reports, and no role for its perpetrators.
rf:refersToAct is limited to confirmations and assurances; no relation for a consequent act building on an earlier one.
No act type for handing over persons (Ministerialen) into another's power or protection distinct from a grant of property.

findings.subject: urn:regesta:22657:transfer
findings.description: The transfer is typed with the generic rv:Grant although the summary states a counter-payment for it ('der dafür 10 Pfund erhält'). The contract has rv:Sale, defined as Übertragung gegen Entgelt, which the passage supports more precisely; the separate payment factoid shows the extractor read the consideration but did not type the main act accordingly. Whether a Tradition with Gegengabe is legally a sale is an expert question, so this is not an error.
findings.evidence_quote: welche die Übergabe zweier Höfe an das Kloster durch Herzog Welf zum Inhalt hat, der dafür 10 Pfund erhält
findings.proposed_correction: Retype to rv:Sale with Welf as rv:Seller and the monastery as rv:Buyer, keeping the payment factoid with rf:partOf; or keep rv:Grant and add rf:qualifier "dafür" so the consideration link stays visible.
